english.title: Returning / presiding officer / clerk administering poll deface / destroy a nomination paper
english.standardoffencewording:

(B)_[the presiding officer]_
(C)_[a clerk appointed to assist in the administration]_

(D)_[of a parliamentary]_
(E)_[local government]_

election at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION OF THE ELECTION..), fraudulently

english.legislation: Contrary to section 65(1)(a) and (3) of the Representation of the People Act 1983.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum. If a returning officer, a presiding officer or a clerk.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time Limit for prosecutions:
NoneNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
